audits.title: 313 Audit of adherence to the National Standards of acute stroke metrics in a tertiary hospital in Dublin, Ireland
audits.standard: 2021 Irish National Audit of Stroke key performance metrics
audits.setting: Tertiary stroke unit, Beaumont Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Thrombolysis rate 18% with 75% receiving tPA within 1 hour of arrival (INAS 10% and 56%); median door-to-image 24 mins and door-to-needle 42 mins (INAS 63 and 43 mins).

audits.citation: Alshehhi S, Durcan R, Lynch J, Liddy A, Boyle K, Williams D, et al.. 313 Audit of adherence to the National Standards of acute stroke metrics in a tertiary hospital in Dublin, Ireland. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.247.

audits.title: Clinical audit of stroke thrombolysis in Wellington, New Zealand: disparity between in-hours and out-of-hours treatment time.
audits.standard: Agreed clinical eligibility criteria for rt-PA

cycle1.result: All treated within eligibility criteria; mean onset-to-treatment 168 minutes; out-of-hours added 33 minutes (p=0.03).

audits.other_findings: Median NIHSS 10 before and 5 after; two deaths from intracranial haemorrhage.
audits.citation: Thorne K, Wong LK, McGonigal G. Clinical audit of stroke thrombolysis in Wellington, New Zealand: disparity between in-hours and out-of-hours treatment time. N Z Med J. 2012;125(1349):30-36. PMID: 22327156.

audits.title: Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) utilisation by rural clinicians in acute ischaemic stroke: an audit of current practice and clinical outcomes.
audits.standard: rt-PA implementation guidelines and treatment protocol
audits.setting: Two rural hospital stroke units, New South Wales, including Wagga Wagga Base Hospital

cycle1.result: 20 (3.3%) received rt-PA; median onset-to-needle 2 h 34 min and door-to-needle 1 h 40 min; no protocol violations; 2 (10%) symptomatic intracranial haemorrhage; one death within 6 months.

audits.other_findings: Morbidity scores were similar in treated and untreated patients; outcomes comparable to metropolitan centres.
audits.citation: Williams JM, Navin TJ, Jude MR, Levi CR. Recombinant tissue plasminogen activator (rt-PA) utilisation by rural clinicians in acute ischaemic stroke: an audit of current practice and clinical outcomes. Aust J Rural Health. 2013;21(4):203-207. doi:10.1111/ajr.12038. PMID: 24033520.

audits.title: The quality of treatment of hyperacute ischemic stroke in Canada: a retrospective chart audit.
audits.standard: Thrombolysis rate as key quality indicator of hyperacute stroke care
audits.setting: Hospitals in 10 Canadian provinces; national chart audit

cycle1.result: 5.4% of stroke and 6.1% of ischaemic stroke patients received thrombolysis; comprehensive stroke centres treated about one-third of ischaemic cases.

audits.other_findings: Thrombolysis often not given (35%-49%) because arrival was over 4.5 hours after onset.
audits.citation: Ganesh A, Camden M, Lindsay P, Kapral MK, Coté R, Fang J, et al.. The quality of treatment of hyperacute ischemic stroke in Canada: a retrospective chart audit. CMAJ Open. 2014;2(4):E233-9. doi:10.9778/cmajo.20140067. PMID: 25485248.

audits.title: Strategies for improving outcomes in the acute management of ischemic stroke in rural emergency departments: a quality improvement initiative in the Stroke Belt.
audits.standard: Guideline door-to-needle time of 60 minutes for alteplase
audits.setting: Emergency departments of 5 non-primary stroke centre rural hospitals in the Stroke Belt

cycle1.result: 1.9% of patients treated with alteplase within 60 minutes of arrival.

audits.intervention: Repeat audit-and-feedback cycles, CME grand rounds at each site and targeted reinforcement of best practice
audits.other_findings: Staff overestimated their door-to-needle performance at baseline.
audits.citation: Jauch EC, Huang DY, Gardner AJ, Blum JL. Strategies for improving outcomes in the acute management of ischemic stroke in rural emergency departments: a quality improvement initiative in the Stroke Belt. Open Access Emerg Med. 2018;10:53-59. doi:10.2147/oaem.s160269. PMID: 29805271.

audits.title: The Dutch Acute Stroke Audit: Benchmarking acute stroke care in the Netherlands.
audits.standard: National acute stroke quality indicators (time to IVT and IAT, outcome registration)
audits.setting: Nationwide Dutch Acute Stroke Audit, all hospitals

cycle1.result: Median door-to-needle time 27 min; median door-to-groin time 66 min

audits.intervention: Nationwide audit with benchmarking of hospitals

cycle2.result: Median door-to-needle time 25 min; median door-to-groin time 64 min

audits.other_findings: 55,854 AIS and 7727 ICH patients registered over 2015-2016; mRS at three months recorded in only 49% of AIS and 45% of ICH patients.
audits.citation: Kuhrij LS, Wouters MW, van den Berg-Vos RM, de Leeuw FE, Nederkoorn PJ. The Dutch Acute Stroke Audit: Benchmarking acute stroke care in the Netherlands. Eur Stroke J. 2018;3(4):361-368. doi:10.1177/2396987318787695. PMID: 31236484.

audits.title: Optimizing Stroke Pathways: An Observational Audit of Door-to-CT Time, Thrombolysis, and Clinical Outcomes.
audits.standard: Door-to-CT within 25 minutes; door-to-needle under 60 minutes

cycle1.result: 201 (64.8%) had CT within 25 minutes; 96 (31.0%) thrombolysed; mean door-to-needle 52.7 ± 14.6 minutes with 71 (74%) under 60 minutes.

audits.other_findings: Favourable outcome (mRS 0-2) in 52.1% thrombolysed vs 33.2% not; symptomatic haemorrhage 6.2%; in-hospital mortality 11.0%.
audits.citation: Farrukh Z, Younas MU, Yousaf A, Nofal S, Kamal Z, Anjum B. Optimizing Stroke Pathways: An Observational Audit of Door-to-CT Time, Thrombolysis, and Clinical Outcomes. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97118. doi:10.7759/cureus.97118. PMID: 41426825.
